title: A Cry of War
summary: After a period of peace in the land of Zarahemla, a cry of war is heard throughout the land.

explicit_facts.text: The cry of war was heard on the fifth day of the second month in the eleventh year of the judges, after a period of peace without wars or contentions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The cry of war may be represented by alarmed people reacting to a distant call.
unspecified_visual_details: Who cries out, the source of the cry, and the exact setting within the land are not specified.

narration.text: there was a cry of war heard throughout the land.

prohibited_inventions: Do not show a battle yet; this verse only reports that a cry of war was heard.

title: The Attack on Ammonihah
summary: Lamanite armies enter the land from the wilderness side, reach Ammonihah, kill people, and destroy the city.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanite armies entered through the wilderness side into the borders of the land and came into Ammonihah.
The armies began killing the people and destroying the city.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The attack may show the Lamanite armies moving into the city as destruction begins.
unspecified_visual_details: The armies' appearance, weapons, number, and the city's architecture are unspecified.

narration.text: began to slay the people and destroy the city.

prohibited_inventions: Do not add named individuals, tactical details, or graphic depictions of injury.

title: Captives Taken into the Wilderness
summary: Before the Nephites can raise a sufficient army, Ammonihah's people are destroyed, some people around Noah's borders are also destroyed, and others are taken captive into the wilderness. The Nephites want to recover the captives.
characters: People around the borders of Noah

explicit_facts.text: Before the Nephites could raise a sufficient army, the people in Ammonihah were destroyed.
Some people around the borders of Noah were destroyed and others were taken captive into the wilderness.
The Nephites desired to recover those carried captive into the wilderness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A single moment may show captives being led away toward the wilderness, while the Nephite response is conveyed through narration.
unspecified_visual_details: The captives' identities, number, and the exact route are unspecified.

narration.text: taken others captive into the wilderness.
the Nephites were desirous to obtain those who had been carried away captive into the wilderness.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The desire to recover the captives is reported; do not depict it as a separate present-time gathering scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Nephite army assembling or a rescue attempt at this point.

title: Zoram Seeks Alma's Direction
summary: Zoram, chief captain of the Nephite armies, and his sons Lehi and Aha go to Alma to ask where the Lord would have them search for their captive brethren.

explicit_facts.text: Zoram was appointed chief captain over the Nephite armies and had two sons, Lehi and Aha.
Zoram and his sons went to Alma, knowing he was high priest and had the spirit of prophecy, and asked where the Lord would have them search for their captive brethren.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The meeting may show Zoram and his sons addressing Alma.
unspecified_visual_details: The meeting place and the appearance of the four men are unspecified.

narration.text: they went unto him and desired of him to know whither the Lord would that they should go into the wilderness in search of their brethren,

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the wording of Zoram's request as direct dialogue.

title: Alma's Answer
summary: Alma inquires of the Lord, then returns and tells the people that the Lamanites will cross the river Sidon and that they will meet them east of the river, where the Lord will deliver the captives.

explicit_facts.text: Alma inquired of the Lord concerning the matter.
Alma returned and spoke to a group of people.
Alma said the Lamanites would cross the river Sidon in the south wilderness, beyond the borders of the land of Manti.
Alma said the people he addressed would meet the Lamanites east of the river Sidon and that the Lord would deliver their captive brethren.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma may be shown addressing the people after his return.
unspecified_visual_details: The location of Alma's return and the appearance of those he addresses are unspecified.
How Alma inquired of the Lord is unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, the Lamanites will cross the river Sidon in the south wilderness, away up beyond the borders of the land of Manti.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma

spoken_dialogue.text: And behold there shall ye meet them, on the east of the river Sidon, and there the Lord will deliver unto thee thy brethren who have been taken captive by the Lamanites.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The crossing, meeting, and deliverance are described as future events, not events occurring during Alma's answer.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the people Alma addresses.
Do not depict the Lord or a visible response; neither is described.
Do not show the predicted crossing, meeting, or deliverance as happening in this scene.

title: Crossing the Sidon
summary: Zoram, his sons, and their armies cross the river Sidon and march beyond Manti into the south wilderness east of the river.

explicit_facts.text: Zoram and his sons crossed the river Sidon with their armies and marched beyond Manti into the south wilderness east of the river.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The crossing and march may be shown as one continuous movement.
unspecified_visual_details: The army's size, clothing, equipment, and river conditions are unspecified.

narration.text: Zoram and his sons crossed over the river Sidon, with their armies,

prohibited_inventions: Do not show combat or captives being recovered in this scene.

title: Captives Recovered
summary: The Nephites encounter the Lamanite armies, scatter and drive them into the wilderness, recover all their captive brethren, and bring them to possess their own lands.

explicit_facts.text: Zoram's party encountered the Lamanite armies, which were scattered and driven into the wilderness.
They recovered every captive taken by the Lamanites; none had been lost.
The captives were brought by their brethren to possess their own lands.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The encounter and dispersal may be shown without graphic violence; captives may be shown reunited with their rescuers.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise sequence of the encounter and recovery, and the identity of the captives, are unspecified.

narration.text: the Lamanites were scattered and driven into the wilderness;
there was not one soul of them had been lost that were taken captive.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The bringing of captives to their lands is reported as the outcome, not a separate scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add deaths or injuries in the battle.

title: Ammonihah Left Desolate
summary: The Lamanites are driven out, and Ammonihah and its people are destroyed. The city is left desolate in one day.

explicit_facts.text: At the end of the eleventh year the Lamanites had been driven out, and every living soul of Ammonihah's people and the great city were destroyed.
Ammonihah was left desolate in one day.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The ruined city may be shown empty and desolate.
unspecified_visual_details: The method by which the city was destroyed and the exact appearance of the ruins are unspecified.

narration.text: in one day it was left desolate;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The chapter reports the city's destruction and aftermath; this scene does not depict individual deaths.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show graphic remains, carcasses, or invented causes of destruction.

title: Desolation of Nehors
summary: After many days, the bodies lie heaped on the land under a shallow covering. The people avoid possessing Ammonihah for many years, and the land remains desolate under the name Desolation of Nehors.

explicit_facts.text: After many days, the dead bodies were heaped on the earth and covered with a shallow covering.
The scent kept people from possessing Ammonihah for many years; the place was called Desolation of Nehors and its lands remained desolate.
The slain people were of the profession of Nehor.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A barren, unoccupied landscape may represent the land remaining desolate.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the shallow covering and the exact landscape are unspecified.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: This describes an aftermath after many days; do not combine it with the attack as if simultaneous.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict bodies graphically; omit visible remains and convey desolation through the abandoned land.

title: Three Years of Peace
summary: The Lamanites do not return to war until the fourteenth year, and the Nephites have continual peace for three years.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites did not again wage war against the Nephites until the fourteenth year of the judges.
The Nephites had continual peace throughout the land for three years.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A peaceful landscape may suggest the reported period of peace.
unspecified_visual_details: Any particular people, activity, or location during this period is unspecified.

narration.text: for three years did the people of Nephi have continual peace in all the land.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a time summary, not a specific event or gathering.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a visible peace celebration or an unreported event.

title: Alma and Amulek Preach
summary: Alma and Amulek preach repentance in temples, sanctuaries, and synagogues; they impart the word of God to all who hear them, without respect of persons.

explicit_facts.text: Alma and Amulek preached repentance in temples, sanctuaries, and synagogues built after the manner of the Jews.
They imparted the word of God continually to all who would hear, without respect of persons.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The preaching may be shown in one supported worship setting, with listeners implied but not individually specified.
unspecified_visual_details: Which specific building hosts a given sermon, the listeners' identities, and the buildings' precise design are unspecified.

narration.text: Alma and Amulek went forth preaching repentance

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses summarize preaching across several kinds of venues; this scene should use one venue, not depict simultaneous sermons in multiple places.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent sermon wording or specific audience members.

title: Preaching Throughout the Land
summary: Alma, Amulek, and others chosen for the work preach throughout the land, and the church becomes generally established among the Nephites.

explicit_facts.text: Alma and Amulek, with many others chosen for the work, preached throughout the land.
The church became generally established throughout the land among the Nephites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A preacher addressing listeners may illustrate the reported preaching, without implying one gathering represents the entire land.
unspecified_visual_details: The other preachers, specific locations, and how the church was established are unspecified.

narration.text: the word throughout all the land.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a summarized spread of preaching, not a single event occurring simultaneously throughout the land.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent named preachers, converts, or a specific establishment ceremony.

title: The People Prepared to Receive the Word
summary: The account says there is no inequality among the people and that the Lord pours out his Spirit to prepare people to receive the word, that they may receive it with joy and enter into the Lord's rest.

explicit_facts.text: There was no inequality among the people.
The Lord poured out his Spirit to prepare the minds and hearts of the children of men to receive the word.
The purpose described is that they not be hardened or unbelieving, but receive the word with joy and enter into the Lord's rest.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People listening to preaching may illustrate the teaching, without showing the Spirit as a visible figure or force.
unspecified_visual_details: The Spirit's visual appearance, any specific listeners, and a visible representation of the Lord's rest are unspecified.

narration.text: there was no inequality among them;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The vine and grafting language is figurative teaching, not a literal scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible divine figure, supernatural spectacle, or literal grafting.

title: Priests Teach Against Wickedness
summary: The priests preach against wrongdoing and teach of things to come, including the coming of the Son of God, his sufferings and death, and the resurrection of the dead.

explicit_facts.text: The priests preached against lying, deception, envy, strife, malice, reviling, stealing, robbery, plundering, murder, adultery, and lasciviousness.
They taught of things to come, the coming of the Son of God, his sufferings and death, and the resurrection of the dead.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A priest teaching an audience may represent the summarized preaching.
unspecified_visual_details: The priests' identities, venue, audience, and the manner of their teaching are unspecified.

narration.text: these things ought not so to be—

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Son of God's future coming and suffering are teachings here, not events occurring in the scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the Son of God, a crucifixion, or resurrection as a present visual event.

title: Questions About the Son of God
summary: Many people ask where the Son of God will come. They are taught that he will appear to them after his resurrection, and they hear this with joy and gladness.

explicit_facts.text: Many people asked where the Son of God would come.
They were taught that he would appear to them after his resurrection, and they heard this with great joy and gladness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Listeners showing joy while receiving instruction may illustrate the reported response.
unspecified_visual_details: The teacher, teaching place, and the Son of God's future appearance are not visually specified.

narration.text: this the people did hear with great joy and gladness.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The promised appearance is future and reported as teaching; do not depict it as happening now.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the location of the Son of God's appearance or show him in this scene.

title: The Fourteenth Year Ends
summary: The account concludes the fourteenth year, reporting that the church has been established throughout the land, the word of God is preached in its purity, and the Lord pours blessings upon the people.

explicit_facts.text: The church had been established throughout the land, the word of God was preached in its purity, and the Lord poured blessings upon the people.
The fourteenth year of the judges ended.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A general view of the land may suggest the account's summary of conditions.
unspecified_visual_details: The form of the Lord's blessings and any specific people or event are unspecified.

narration.text: thus ended the fourteenth year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Victory over the devil is a figurative or spiritual summary, not a literal combat scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the devil or a literal battle with him.
